[SCENE] Unregistered third-party truck enters a marked restricted industrial zone; show detection, alarm, and security response

[APPLICATION] Industrial use case: safety_training. Application objective: Train or evaluate recognition of unsafe industrial states, violations, alarms, and required safe responses. Scenario: Unregistered third-party truck enters a marked restricted industrial zone; show detection, alarm, and security response. Required observable events: the unsafe trigger or violation is visually present: industrial gate vehicle restricted zone; the relevant alarm, stop, warning, or protective response is visible; the final state shows whether the hazard is contained or still active. Decision-relevant elements: worker or vehicle position relative to the danger zone (industrial gate vehicle restricted zone); PPE, barrier, signage, interlock, or alarm state; machine state before and after the trigger; reference-image requirement: Gate, loading dock, factory road, or restricted lane with clear vehicle path and access boundary. Usable only if: a safety reviewer can identify the violation and the required response; the event sequence is complete enough for training or compliance audit; the clip does not invent misleading safe states after a hazardous trigger.

[CAMERA] STATIC: camera locked, zero movement throughout.

[EVENT_LOOP] Complete event loop: 1) Reference-anchored stable industrial scene showing industrial gate vehicle restricted zone before the event.; 2) trigger: an unsafe act, violation, or hazardous proximity involving industrial gate vehicle restricted zone; 3) progression: the unsafe trigger or violation is visually present: industrial gate vehicle restricted zone: Unregistered third-party truck enters a marked restricted industrial zone; show detection, alarm, and security response; visible event progression remains localized and causally ordered for industrial gate vehicle restricted zone; 4) response: the relevant alarm, stop, warning, or protective response is visible; 5) final state: the final state shows whether the hazard is contained or still active; critical industrial decision: whether the unsafe state and required safe response are clear enough for training or compliance review.

[EVENT] Show: Unregistered third-party truck enters a marked restricted industrial zone; show detection, alarm, and security response Common failure modes to AVOID: identity_swap; global_scene_regeneration; implausible_motion_or_flow. Require a complete causal chain: trigger -> system response -> resolved state, all within 5 seconds.

[PRESERVE] Subject identity: industrial gate vehicle restricted zone. Component counts must remain constant in all non-failure regions. Background, lighting, and layout must stay identical to the reference image. Material textures, surface markings, and color must not drift between frames.

[PROHIBIT] No text overlays, subtitles, logos, or watermarks. No extra machines, vehicles, or people appearing without cause. No geometry warping, melting, or flickering. No identity swaps or model changes mid-clip. No impossible physics: floating loads, rigid bodies bending, penetration, or unsupported motion. No global scene regeneration; changes must stay local to the specified event zone.

samples.application_objective: Simulate rare industrial emergency evolution for response planning, drills, and hazard communication. Scenario: Smoke emerges from equipment, alarm triggers, and workers evacuate following a plausible causal chain.
required_observable_events: the initiating fault or release point is identifiable: industrial corridor smoke alarm
the hazard propagation direction and growth are visible over time
the scene preserves containment, evacuation, or escalation cues
decision_relevant_elements: leak, smoke, fire, flood, collapse, or blast source (industrial corridor smoke alarm)
nearby workers, vehicles, barriers, exits, valves, or emergency devices
spatial relation between hazard path and assets at risk
reference-image requirement: Industrial corridor, workshop, battery room, or equipment bay with alarm/exit context
application_success_criteria: an emergency planner can infer likely propagation and immediate action
the simulated dynamics follow plausible physics and industrial causality
critical landmarks stay stable enough to support route or containment decisions
misleading_failure_modes: hazard teleports, disappears, or expands against plausible direction
containment or evacuation cues are missing despite being decision critical
global scene regeneration breaks situational awareness

[SCENE] Worker crosses light curtain; robot or machine performs emergency stop and remains stopped

[APPLICATION] Industrial use case: robotic_operation. Application objective: Evaluate whether generated robot or machine operation videos preserve actionable geometry, contact, and task progress. [CAMERA] STATIC: camera locked, zero movement throughout.

[SCENE] Overloaded wire rope deforms and snaps locally; unchanged crane/load regions stay locked to reference

[APPLICATION] Industrial use case: heavy_operation_risk. Application objective: Assess whether heavy equipment, loads, supports, and worksite risks evolve plausibly for planning and supervision. Scenario: Overloaded wire rope deforms and snaps locally; unchanged crane/load regions stay locked to reference. Required observable events: load, machine, support, worker, or worksite risk source is visible: crane wire rope hook block; the requested operation or failure progression occurs; final risk state is clear enough to judge stability or escalation. Decision-relevant elements: load path, rigging, outrigger, support, ground, or bridge alignment (crane wire rope hook block); clearance to workers, vehicles, obstacles, or exclusion zones; motion direction, contact points, and structural deformation cues; reference-image requirement: Crane wire rope, sling, hoist cable, or hook block with visible tension path. Usable only if: a site engineer can infer whether the operation remains safe; gravity, support, load transfer, and contact are physically credible; critical geometry and worksite context stay stable across frames.

[CAMERA] DOLLY FORWARD into the scene along the central axis, starting from the reference-image viewpoint. Maintain subject framing throughout.

[EVENT_LOOP] Complete event loop: 1) Reference-anchored stable industrial scene showing crane wire rope hook block before the event.; 2) trigger: a load, support, clearance, ground, or structural-risk change involving crane wire rope hook block; 3) progression: load, machine, support, worker, or worksite risk source is visible: crane wire rope hook block: Overloaded wire rope deforms and snaps locally; unchanged crane/load regions stay locked to reference; visible event progression remains localized and causally ordered for crane wire rope hook block; 4) response: the requested operation or failure progression occurs; 5) final state: final risk state is clear enough to judge stability or escalation; critical industrial decision: whether the worksite risk, load path, support state, and personnel distance can be judged.

[EVENT] Show: Overloaded wire rope deforms and snaps locally; unchanged crane/load regions stay locked to reference Common failure modes to AVOID: identity_swap; global_scene_regeneration; implausible_motion_or_flow. The specified structural change must be localized to the failure zone. All surrounding geometry remains stable.

[PRESERVE] Subject identity: crane wire rope hook block. Component counts must remain constant in all non-failure regions. Background, lighting, and layout must stay identical to the reference image. Material textures, surface markings, and color must not drift between frames.

[PROHIBIT] No text overlays, subtitles, logos, or watermarks. No extra machines, vehicles, or people appearing without cause. No geometry warping, melting, or flickering. No identity swaps or model changes mid-clip. No impossible physics: floating loads, rigid bodies bending, penetration, or unsupported motion. No global scene regeneration; changes must stay local to the specified event zone.

Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Formwork, scaffold, temporary support, shoring tower, or concrete pouring support. Scenario: One gear tooth chips or wears severely; tooth count and neighboring geometry remain stable. No global scene regeneration; changes must stay local to the specified event zone.

Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Press line, automated machine row, robot cell, or safeguarded industrial workstation with reachable operating area. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Required observable events: automated machine, press line, or safeguarded operating area is visible; worker entry or hand proximity to the operating area is visible; machine remains stopped or enters protective stop until the area is clear. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Industrial retaining wall, tailings dam face, containment berm, or flood barrier. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. [SCENE] Local breach forms in containment wall and water/slurry escapes through the opening with plausible erosion

[APPLICATION] Industrial use case: emergency_rehearsal. Application objective: Simulate rare industrial emergency evolution for response planning, drills, and hazard communication. Scenario: Local breach forms in containment wall and water/slurry escapes through the opening with plausible erosion. Required observable events: the initiating fault or release point is identifiable: industrial retaining wall containment berm; the hazard propagation direction and growth are visible over time; the scene preserves containment, evacuation, or escalation cues. Decision-relevant elements: leak, smoke, fire, flood, collapse, or blast source (industrial retaining wall containment berm); nearby workers, vehicles, barriers, exits, valves, or emergency devices; spatial relation between hazard path and assets at risk; reference-image requirement: Industrial retaining wall, tailings dam face, containment berm, or flood barrier. Usable only if: an emergency planner can infer likely propagation and immediate action; the simulated dynamics follow plausible physics and industrial causality; critical landmarks stay stable enough to support route or containment decisions.

[CAMERA] DOLLY FORWARD into the scene along the central axis, starting from the reference-image viewpoint. Maintain subject framing throughout.

[EVENT_LOOP] Complete event loop: 1) Reference-anchored stable industrial scene showing industrial retaining wall containment berm before the event.; 2) trigger: an initiating emergency fault or release at industrial retaining wall containment berm; 3) progression: the initiating fault or release point is identifiable: industrial retaining wall containment berm: Local breach forms in containment wall and water/slurry escapes through the opening with plausible erosion; visible event progression remains localized and causally ordered for industrial retaining wall containment berm; 4) response: the hazard propagation direction and growth are visible over time; 5) final state: the scene preserves containment, evacuation, or escalation cues; critical industrial decision: whether the hazard source, propagation path, and immediate response cues are clear enough for rehearsal planning.

[EVENT] Show: Local breach forms in containment wall and water/slurry escapes through the opening with plausible erosion Common failure modes to AVOID: identity_swap; global_scene_regeneration; implausible_motion_or_flow. The specified structural change must be localized to the failure zone. All surrounding geometry remains stable.

[PRESERVE] Subject identity: industrial retaining wall containment berm. Component counts must remain constant in all non-failure regions. Background, lighting, and layout must stay identical to the reference image. Material textures, surface markings, and color must not drift between frames.

[PROHIBIT] No text overlays, subtitles, logos, or watermarks. No extra machines, vehicles, or people appearing without cause. No geometry warping, melting, or flickering. No identity swaps or model changes mid-clip. No impossible physics: floating loads, rigid bodies bending, penetration, or unsupported motion. No global scene regeneration; changes must stay local to the specified event zone.

Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Formwork, scaffold, temporary support, shoring tower, or concrete pouring support. Image requirement: Gantry crane, container crane, bridge crane, or large portal frame in open yard. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object.
